name: Enrichment, Peer Tutoring, and Group Work
title: Enrichment, Peer Tutoring, and Group Work
answer: Personalization in AI ready schools is not only for students who are behind. Students who are ready for more can use AI to explore topics in greater depth, tackle harder problems, or pursue independent projects, and AI can also support peer tutoring and group work. The teacher keeps the final say on pairings, enrichment tasks, and group structures.

sections.body: This idea extends personalized learning beyond remediation to enrichment, peer tutoring, and group projects. Students who are ready for more can use AI to go deeper into topics, take on harder problems, or pursue independent work, while a teacher generates enrichment tasks and checks them for accuracy and challenge. Peer tutoring pairs students so they learn from each other, with AI features in a spreadsheet suggesting pairings based on skills that the teacher then adjusts using knowledge of personalities and friendships. Group projects can also draw on AI support, with tools that help groups plan, divide work, and reflect on how well they worked together. The problem it solves is that personalization can otherwise be treated as something only for students who are behind, leaving advanced students and collaborative work without the same support.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a classroom, a teacher can generate enrichment tasks for students who are ready for more and then check those tasks for accuracy and challenge before handing them out. These students also benefit from the hint only approach, since they learn more from struggling with a hard problem than from being handed the answer. For peer tutoring, a teacher can use AI features in a spreadsheet to suggest pairings based on skills, then adjust the pairs using what they know about personalities and friendships, and the teacher makes the final pairings. For group projects, a teacher can use AI to draft planning templates and role descriptions for groups, while the group does the work and the thinking, with AI helping them organize. The text does not give grade band variations for these practices.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text offers one evidence label for the group work part of this idea. It states that a review of AI agents in collaborative learning describes tools that help groups plan, divide work, and reflect on how well they worked together (Ba et al., 2026). No study, figure, or finding is given for the enrichment or peer tutoring parts of the idea, so those rest on practice rather than research as the text presents them.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The teacher keeps several decisions that stay with a person. A teacher who generates enrichment tasks must check them for accuracy and challenge rather than assume they are suitable. The teacher makes the final peer tutoring pairings, adjusting any AI suggested pairings using what they know about personalities and friendships. In group projects, the group does the work and the thinking, with AI only helping them organize, so the intellectual work is not handed over to the tool. The text does not set out further limits, risks, or legal rules, and nothing here is legal advice.
